Guitar FX Layouts: VFE Pedals Dragon Hound Guitar FX Layouts Here's a collection of vero (stripboard) and tagboard guitar and bass effect layouts that we have put together covering many classic and popular effects in growing numbers. Many of these have been posted on freestompboxes.org, so check that site out for great discussions on building your own effect pedals. Enjoy the builds and please also visit us on Facebook and Twitter Pages Home Layout Guide Components Build Guide Offboard Faults Kits Forum Site Map NEW Monday, 6 November 2017 VFE Pedals Dragon Hound " The DRAGON HOUND is a dual overdrive + distortion pedal that combines the core circuits from the Alpha Dog and Pale Horse into one unique dirt box. Each circuit has a dedicated drive control, and the blend control can dial in saturated distortion tones that retain the clarity of an overdrive. " You can find their original pedal (now discontinued) on their website  here and the original schematic here . Posted by Alex at 16:01 Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook Share to Pinterest Tags: Difficult , Distortion , Hound , Overdrive , Verified , Vero , VFE 12 comments: Hozy31 6 November 2017 at 16:33 That was quick. Only just saw the request. Nice layout. Must build soon. Cheers Alex! Reply Delete Replies Reply Claudio 7 November 2017 at 13:38 seeing this i was wondeimg how can i add a blend pot for dual offboard wiring? Reply Delete Replies Alex 7 November 2017 at 15:54 The A-P pot is a "Blend" between the Alpha Dog and the Pale Horse. What do you mean a Blend for dual offboard wiring? Delete Replies Reply Claudio 8 November 2017 at 02:46 imagine you have 2 effects, in one box with 2 switches, you can have use one at the time, or both effects on, (1 Ts and 2 fuzz face) I want a blend pot for mix both pedals, the pot in middle position is both eefects mixed to the right ts only and to the left the sound of fuzz face, thats the idea Delete Replies Reply Unknown 9 November 2017 at 05:52 I THINK with pedals that have equal and low output impedance (they have to be pretty much equal) you will be able to get away with just a simple passive blend (essentially a pot of the right size). For everything else you will need a buffered (active) blend like e.g. the splitter-blend of rog is using http://runoffgroove.com/splitter-blend.html Delete Replies Reply Reply glasspak73 12 November 2017 at 00:41 Is it possible to substitute two B5k pots inplace of the B10k A.P pot? I'm thinking this would give more blending options of the two circuits.I'm building this circuit now and plan to try this out if anyone is interested in the results? Reply Delete Replies Reply glasspak73 14 November 2017 at 20:16 I have the board built and populated now just have to wire it up today.soon as i get some sounds out of it i'll report back.Hope this helps Reply Delete Replies Reply glasspak73 15 November 2017 at 00:32 OK I have built this almost exact to this vero layout.Only thing i changed is the Comp trim is now a B100k pot.Row two is leg 3 on comp pot and row three is leg 2 on the comp pot.So this is verified now,Thank you very very much Alex.I have built the Plimsoul befor this but i think this circuit is soooo much better sounding.I'm going to try replacing the A-P pot with two B5k pots and see if this mod will work.Thanks again Alex and everyone involved Reply Delete Replies Alex 15 November 2017 at 15:48 Thanks Chris! Delete Replies Reply Reply glasspak73 23 November 2017 at 14:56 I'm still in the tweaking process with this circuit.for some reason the Alpha Dog side on my build doesnt seem to be as loud as the Pale Horse side.I'm working on a way to correct this.I'll post my results asap. Reply Delete Replies Reply Mr.Baiser 10 December 2017 at 10:52 Thanx a lot for this layout! (I wrote the request...) I will build this as a present for a friend :-) Reply Delete Replies Reply glasspak73 10 December 2017 at 14:57 I added two B5k pots inplace of the one B10k A-P pot.Now i can
